abstract: As Transfer Learning from large-scale pre-trained models becomes more prevalent in Natural Language Processing (NLP), operating these large models in on-the-edge and/or under constrained computational training or inference budgets remains challenging. In this work, we propose a method to pre-train a smaller general-purpose language representation model, called DistilBERT, which can then be fine-tuned with good performances on a wide range of tasks like its larger counterparts. While most prior work investigated the use of distillation for building task-specific models, we leverage knowledge distillation during the pre-training phase and show that it is possible to reduce the size of a BERT model by 40%, while retaining 97% of its language understanding capabilities and being 60% faster. To leverage the inductive biases learned by larger models during pre-training, we introduce a triple loss combining language modeling, distillation and cosine-distance losses. Our smaller, faster and lighter model is cheaper to pre-train and we demonstrate its capabilities for on-device computations in a proof-of-concept experiment and a comparative on-device study.

bibliographic.title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter

content.problem: Growing parameter counts in pre-trained language models inflate computational and memory costs, hindering deployment on edge devices and under constrained operational budgets.
content.proposed_solution: The authors pre-train a smaller general-purpose model, DistilBERT, from a BERT teacher with a triple loss that combines masked language modeling, distillation, and cosine-distance objectives.
dataset_testbed: English Wikipedia and Toronto Book Corpus (pre-training corpus)
Intel Xeon E5-2690 v3 CPU (inference timing)

metrics.name: percentage of BERT performance retained
metrics.condition: DistilBERT versus BERT-base macro-score on the GLUE dev sets

metrics.name: parameter reduction
metrics.condition: DistilBERT (66M parameters) relative to BERT-base (110M parameters)

metrics.name: inference speed-up
metrics.condition: full inference pass on the GLUE STS-B dev set on CPU with a batch size of 1

metrics.name: GLUE macro-score
metrics.condition: DistilBERT, median of 5 runs with different seeds, on the GLUE dev sets

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.condition: DistilBERT on the IMDb sentiment classification test set

metrics.name: F1
metrics.condition: DistilBERT fine-tuned on SQuAD 1.1, dev set

metrics.name: exact match (EM)
metrics.condition: DistilBERT fine-tuned on SQuAD 1.1, dev set

metrics.name: F1
metrics.condition: DistilBERT with an additional distillation step during fine-tuning on SQuAD 1.1

metrics.name: on-device inference speed-up
metrics.condition: question answering application on iPhone 7 Plus versus a BERT-base model, excluding tokenization

metrics.name: model size
metrics.condition: DistilBERT question answering model prepared for on-device use

content.claim: Knowledge distillation during pre-training produces a 40% smaller and 60% faster general-purpose model that retains 97% of BERT's language understanding performance and supports on-device use.
